transcript:
This message comes from Capital One with the Venture X card.
Earn unlimited double-miles and a $300 annual Capital One travel credit.
Capital One.
What's in your wallet?
Terms of fly.
Details at CapitalOne.com.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
A commercial flight from Dubai in the United Arab Emirates to Tel Aviv in Israel made an
emergency landing in Saudi Arabia this morning after one of the pilots stabbed the other
pilot and was apparently trying to crash the plane with everyone on board.
The incident is still under investigation as NPR's Kat Lonsdorf reports.
Israeli officials are calling this an attempted terrorist attack, but a statement put out by
Fly Dubai urged caution on that, saying that the motives behind the incident are unknown
and remain subject to a formal investigation.
This all comes at a particularly political time here in Israel, as national elections
are less than a month away.
Those elections will determine whether Netanyahu remains prime minister.
He's been campaigning on this idea that he alone can protect Israelis from the threats
that Israel faces.
So this incident on the plane will almost certainly be a talking point in the coming
weeks as that election grows closer.
NPR's Kat Lonsdorf reporting.
President Trump is insisting that his party can win in November this year, bucking the
long-documented trend that the party in power tends to see losses in the midterm elections.
Speaking at a Hispanic Heritage Month celebration, Trump said the economy is doing well and encouraged
people to vote, as NPR's Deepa Shivaram reports.
Trump told supporters at the White House, even if they don't love their Republican candidate,
the alternative would be worse.
Even if you don't like somebody so much, it doesn't matter, it's a vote for good things,
you know?
It's hard to explain that, but you may not love your Congressperson, your Senate, but
it's a road like in Michigan.
Are you going to vote for a guy who's a communist?
That was a dig at Democratic Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El Sayed, who's in his party's
left flank but is not a communist or Democratic socialist.
Trump plans to campaign in Texas this week and has said he'll also make stops in Iowa
and Alaska later on.
Deepa Shivaram, NPR News, The White House.
An internal watchdog says management shortcomings at the Federal Reserve contributed to cost
overruns on the central bank's headquarters renovation, but as NPR's Scott Horsley reports,
the inspector general found no sign of deliberate misconduct, let alone criminal wrongdoing.
The renovation of the Federal Reserve's headquarters is years behind schedule and more than a billion
dollars over budget.
After similar cost overruns with an earlier project, the Fed had promised a different
approach that was supposed to shift more responsibility for staying within budget onto a private construction
manager.
The inspector general found Fed officials did not follow through with that plan.
Design changes, inflation and a lack of competitive bids also contributed to the rising price tag.
The Trump administration had launched a criminal probe of the project, but a federal judge
pulled the plug on that investigation, calling it part of an improper pressure campaign to
get the Fed to lower interest rates.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
Most U.S. stocks fell today.
The S&P 500 slipped a quarter percent.
The Dow fell more than three quarters of a percent.
But the NASDAQ composite climbed nearly a quarter percent.
This is NPR News from Washington.
Russia has warned NATO it could use nuclear weapons to defend Kaliningrad if allies attempt
to cut off the exclave.
The warning follows claims by Russian embassies in Europe that NATO is prepping a blockade
of the region.
Kaliningrad is located between NATO members Poland and Lithuania, and is home to Russia's
main Baltic Navy base.
NATO has conducted military exercises in the Baltic Sea region recently, and NATO's spokesperson
criticized Russia's "irresponsible" use of nuclear rhetoric.
The nation's largest public transit system says President Trump's tariffs are making
it harder to repair and replace New York trains and buses, Steve Kastenbaum reports.
The Metropolitan Transit Authority is acquiring thousands of new subway cars and buses at
a cost of $23 billion.
Around a billion of that is for tariffs on components made overseas, according to Jan
O'Leber, who runs the agency.
He spoke about the added cost at a recent Citizens Budget Commission event.
The result is the federal dollars that go into buying rail cars deliver fewer jobs and
fewer rail cars.
Now, Governor Kathy Hochul is demanding that the White House exempt them from tariffs on
components needed to manufacture trains and buses.
The White House fired back, accusing the Transit Authority of chronic mismanagement and cost
overruns.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Kastenbaum in New York.
A dozen impressionists and post-impressionists' artworks valued at almost half a billion dollars
are going up for auction.
Sotheby's says that works by Vincent van Gogh and Paul Cezanne are expected to smash records
in the November 18 sale in New York.
This is NPR News.
